title: A trusted neighbourhood support plan
label: DOCUMENTS & SUPPORT
deck: Build a small support network with people you already trust: agree check-ins, practical tasks and boundaries before a crisis. Share verified information and safe assistance without advertising stockpiles or exposing vulnerable people’s locations. Do not organise untrained rescues or assume outside supplies will arrive.
tldr: Build a small support network with people you already trust: agree check-ins, practical tasks and boundaries before a crisis. Share verified information and safe assistance without advertising stockpiles or exposing vulnerable people’s locations. Do not organise untrained rescues or assume outside supplies will arrive.
steps: Ask consent and include people who may need help with movement, medication or communication. Do not publish a public list of vulnerable households.
Choose check-in, charging, water transport or childcare tasks people can perform safely. Do not assign dangerous repairs, rescues or conflict-zone travel.
Have another contact and a written way to reconnect if phones fail. Make sure no essential task depends on one person being present.
Agree what can be shared, how decisions are made and what people cannot safely offer. Do not promise supplies or transport you do not have.
Practise a short check-in and update the plan after household needs change. Keep information current and private.
next: Use the network to coordinate verified information and reduce duplicated trips. Independent humanitarian assistance can complement it when available, but should not be its only foundation.
watch: Mutual aid should never require handing over identity documents, leaving children with strangers or entering a dangerous building.
without_help: Start with a few trusted people and one useful task. If no network exists, use your household plan and independently verify any offer before relying on it.
household: Assign a trusted adult to each person who needs assistance. Keep medicines, essential contacts and a workable reunion plan with the group. Make decisions around the least mobile person, not the fastest; avoid splitting the family without a clear, safe way to reconnect.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, safe drinking water, a battery light, footwear, phone power and written contacts accessible. Carry only what you can manage; collecting supplies must not delay escape.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
